title: Choose One Signal for May
teaser: A month becomes easier to steer when one useful signal is tracked consistently.
full_text: Pick one measure to watch through May. Write what it represents and which behavior you can realistically influence rather than treating the number as a goal by itself.

title: Label Why the Work Is Waiting
teaser: A stalled task becomes easier to move when the actual blocker is named.
full_text: Choose three waiting tasks today and classify each blocker as decision, information, time, person, or resource. Set the next action from the blocker instead of from the task title.

title: Turn Notes Into Retrieval Questions
teaser: Questions make learning easier to test than passive notes do.
full_text: Create three short questions from something you learned recently. Hide the answers and try to recall them later before reopening the source.

title: Count the Time Cost of a Purchase
teaser: A low price can hide repeated maintenance, search, or replacement time.
full_text: For one product or service you use often, estimate the time it consumes in addition to money. Use both costs when comparing the next realistic option.

title: Separate Context From the Ask
teaser: Important requests are easier to act on when background and action are not mixed together.
full_text: Write one important message today in two parts: brief context first, explicit request second. Remove details that do not help either part.

title: Find the Most Fragile Step
teaser: A process often fails at a single transition more than across every step equally.
full_text: Review one repeated workflow and identify where errors or delays happen most often. Put one small check at that point before redesigning everything else.

title: Schedule Capacity, Not Just Tasks
teaser: Empty calendar space can be useful operating capacity rather than unused time.
full_text: Add one real buffer block to the next seven days. Protect it for delay, recovery, or unexpected work instead of filling it immediately with another commitment.

title: Connect Appreciation to Impact
teaser: Recognition is more useful when the contribution and its effect are both visible.
full_text: Thank someone today by naming what they did and what it made easier, faster, safer, or clearer. Keep the message concrete rather than exaggerated.

title: Mark Outdated Information Clearly
teaser: Old content can look current when it stays beside newer information without a status label.
full_text: Open one shared document and identify a section that is no longer current. Remove it if appropriate or label its date and status so readers do not treat it as active guidance.

title: Choose an Early Warning Signal
teaser: A risk is easier to manage when you know what small sign appears before the full problem.
full_text: For one important risk, define a single early indicator you can actually observe. Write the small action you will take if that signal appears.

title: Explain It Simply Before You Review It
teaser: The parts you cannot explain often reveal where understanding is still thin.
full_text: Describe one recent concept in plain language without looking at your notes. Mark where the explanation becomes vague, then review only that part.

title: Give a Habit a Clear Starting Cue
teaser: A vague intention is easier to postpone than a behavior attached to a specific event.
full_text: Link one habit today to a concrete cue such as finishing breakfast, opening your desk, or ending a meeting. Replace 'when I have time' with an observable trigger.

title: Set a Deadline for Gathering Evidence
teaser: More information is not always better if the decision never closes.
full_text: For one pending decision, write what evidence you still need and the date when collection stops. Extend only if genuinely critical information appears.

title: Ask How the Other Person Sees the Impact
teaser: Feedback is stronger when observation and self-assessment can be compared.
full_text: Before giving feedback today, ask how the other person thinks the outcome affected the work or relationship. Add your observation afterward and agree on one next behavior.

title: Rechoose the Priority for the Rest of May
teaser: The most useful priority can change as conditions change.
full_text: Review the remaining weeks of May and choose the one priority with the highest current value. Reorder lower-value work around protecting it.

title: Surface the Unspoken Success Criteria
teaser: Shared work can drift when people are using different definitions of a good result.
full_text: For one collaborative task, compare what success means to each person before delivery. Resolve differences while changes are still inexpensive.

title: Check the Cost of Leaving
teaser: A service can be cheap to enter and expensive to leave in time, data, or migration effort.
full_text: Before committing to one product or service, review cancellation terms, export options, and switching effort. Include exit cost in the decision, not only the starting price.

title: Write the Conditions That Allowed the Error
teaser: Preventing a repeat is easier when the enabling conditions are visible.
full_text: Take one recent mistake and list the process, environment, or missing check that made it possible. Change one condition instead of reducing the lesson to personal blame.

title: Remove False Urgency From One Reply
teaser: Not every incoming request deserves an immediate interruption.
full_text: Before answering one message today, confirm the actual deadline. If it is not urgent, choose a response time that protects focused work without leaving the sender uncertain.

title: End a Busy Day With a Shutdown List
teaser: Open loops feel lighter when their next steps are captured outside your head.
full_text: Before finishing work today, write the next action for three unfinished items. Close the workspace after the list exists instead of continuing to carry the tasks mentally.

title: Check What the Metric Actually Means
teaser: The same word can represent different definitions across sources.
full_text: Choose one important term or metric you are using and read its formal definition in the source. Record the definition if it differs from how you have been using it.

title: Put a Boundary on the Calendar
teaser: A boundary that exists only in intention is easier to override when pressure rises.
full_text: Schedule one protected block for rest, focus, or personal time today. Treat it as a commitment with a purpose rather than as unused space.

title: Change One Variable at a Time
teaser: When many conditions change together, it becomes hard to know what caused the result.
full_text: Run one small experiment today with a single deliberate change. Keep the other important conditions as stable as possible and record what happens.

title: Add a Short Checklist to Repeated Work
teaser: A template helps structure output; a checklist helps prevent omission.
full_text: Create a checklist of no more than five critical checks for one repeated task. Keep it short enough that you will actually use it every time.

title: Inspect How the Sample Was Chosen
teaser: A correct calculation can still mislead when the sample systematically leaves important cases out.
full_text: Pick one metric you rely on and examine how its examples or records were selected. Ask whether excluded cases could change the interpretation.

title: Shrink the Work Before the Focus Block
teaser: A task that is too large can delay the first useful output.
full_text: Reduce one focused task to something you can finish in a single session. Keep the larger objective visible, but complete only the first concrete piece today.

title: Name the Need Under the Reaction
teaser: A fast reaction can hide the need you are actually trying to protect.
full_text: When something frustrates you today, write the underlying need before choosing a response. Then generate more than one way to meet that need.

title: Prepare the Second Route
teaser: Plans that depend on one path can stop completely when a small obstacle appears.
full_text: Choose the most likely obstacle in one important plan and define a simple fallback route. Keep the backup proportional rather than building an entire second project.

title: Define the Problem With Evidence
teaser: A problem is easier to improve when its presence can be observed rather than only felt.
full_text: Write two observable signs that show one problem is happening. After making a change, look for movement in those same signs before declaring success.

title: Define Acceptance Before Delegating
teaser: Delegation works better when completion has a shared meaning.
full_text: For one task you hand off today, specify the output, deadline, and acceptance criteria. Ask the other person to confirm the expectation in their own words.

title: Close May With One Reusable Lesson
teaser: A useful monthly review preserves what should influence the next month, not only what was completed.
full_text: Choose one lesson from May that you want to reuse. Identify a specific situation in the first week of June where you will apply it.
